newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Hashimoto says Japan economic fundamentals not bad.
newsitem.headline: Hashimoto says Japan economic fundamentals not bad.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, commenting on recent weakness in Tokyo stock prices, said on Monday that Japan's economic fundamentals are not bad.

Hashimoto, speaking in Singapore on the last stop of a Southeast Asian trip, told a news conference that his government will continue to take proper economic measures including early passage of an extra budget through parliament.
"When we think about Japan's economic fundamentals, they are not bad at all," Hashimoto said.
The Japanese economy is recovering gradually and is expected to continue its moderate recovery, he said.
"We expect domestic demand supported by firming private consumption and capital spending to lead the gradual economic recovery," he said.
Hashimoto said it was difficult to determine the real causes of the recent plunge in Tokyo stock prices, as shares are freely traded in the market.
"It is important for Japan to positively carry out various reforms in a bid to achieve stable and sustainable economic growth led by domestic demand," Hashimoto said.
On the Tokyo stock market, the key Nikkei average of 225 leading shares soared 815.14 points to end at 18,118.79 on Monday, rebounding from losses of over 2,000 points last week.
